## TL;DR

The full check profile completed in 821s: 781s remote validation plus a 39.98s local plan. Remote test time fell from 860.35s to 676.91s (21.3%), below the 25% aim; the dominant dev-targets and remote-host-pool files stayed flat and remain with the parallel #1118 scope. After review, I replaced the fixed watcher setup delay with event-driven retries in both affected watcher suites. Two consecutive full-suite runs on the final implementation passed (708 files, 9,519 passed, 8 skipped each), and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed. Gate steps and assertions remain intact.

## Work and rationale

### Measurement

I profiled `repoos check --profile full` on the configured `thinkpad` runner and captured Vitest file and case markers. A successful pre-change run saved local phase timings: format 2.280s, lint 0.468s, build 13.411s, rendered contrast 17.636s, UI smoke 5.161s; the local plan took 46.548s. The full suite ran remotely first.

A captured baseline retry measured remote validation at 953.816s; tests took 860.35s (707 files passed, one `agent-review` assertion failed, 14 skipped), so it stopped before local steps. RepoOS did not persist the successful baseline's remote duration separately: the runner reports remote validation as one phase, not distinct remote build and test times. The test duration is the explicit before measure; its failure is noted.

The passing after profile measured remote validation at 781s. Vitest passes took 673.30s and 3.61s (676.91s total). The local plan took 39.98s: format 3.300s, lint 0.189s, build 0.098s, contrast 19.263s, UI smoke 6.596s; all checks passed. Total was 820.98s (13m41s). A prior attempt passed remote tests and contrast but remote smoke exited silently; retry and local smoke passed. After scope review removed the pressure-guard edits, final-tree full-suite attempts hit load-sensitive timeouts in unrelated tests: the first had two failing files, and the next had only `check-docs-only-cli.test.ts` timing out at 30s. That test passed alone in 1.58s; the required changed-path RepoOS check passed on the final tree.

| Phase | Before | After | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Remote full test suite | 860.35s | 676.91s | Before attempt had one unrelated `agent-review` failure; after passed |
| Format | 2.280s | 3.300s | Local plan |
| Lint | 0.468s | 0.189s | Local plan |
| Build | 13.411s | 0.098s | Local build was fresh after remote build |
| Rendered contrast | 17.636s | 19.263s | Local plan; remote audit also passed |
| UI smoke | 5.161s | 6.596s | Local plan; passed |
| Full profile wall time | ~15m, successful first run | 13m41s | Baseline total is approximate; see persistence note above |

The test phase improved 21.3%, below the 25% aim. Direct after-suite runs took 264.64s and 328.75s; runner load makes the remote delta noisy, so it cannot all be attributed to code.

### Behaviour-preserving changes

- `agent-contract.test.ts` fake harnesses exit after completed one-shot output. A marker keeps the cancellation child alive until the existing signal assertion stops it. All contract seams remain tested; only a one-second fixture hold was removed. File time: 20.86s→2.40s.
- The Git ref and repo-status watcher tests retry meaningful file changes and wait for the existing debounced signal. If native registration misses an early event, a later distinct write exercises the same assertion. This removes the fixed 50 ms setup guess without weakening the signal checks or adding normal-path delay.

Before/after file seconds: `dev-targets` 144.44/143.84; `remote-host-pool` 54.58/54.49; `agent-review` 25.42/9.52; `handoff` 15.47/5.72; `agent-contract` 20.86/2.40; `task-watchdog` 18.10/18.00. `agent-review` and `handoff` shifts are unexplained run variation. The two largest files stayed flat; their cases exercise real teardown, host locks, and deadlines.

Baseline slowest 15 files (seconds): `dev-targets` 144.44; `remote-host-pool` 54.58; `agent-review` 25.42; `agent-contract` 20.86; `task-watchdog` 18.10; `page-height-browser` 16.66; `handoff` 15.47; `preview-config` 14.27; `remote-validation` 14.07; `reload` 13.69; `activity-indicator-motion` 12.87; `engineer-crash-recovery` 11.01; `skill-suggestion-trigger` 8.89; `done-guard-orchestrator` 8.53; `local-resource-gates` 7.62. All are under `src/ui-app/tests/`.

### Slowest cases

Baseline slowest 15 cases: host-lock absolute deadline 20.01s; watchdog auto-resume after retries 9.80s; two-process lock serialization 5.51s; orphan-lock recovery 5.01s; lock heartbeat 5.01s; six dev-target service/target teardown cases 4.81–4.82s; agent-review freeze 4.59s; watchdog same-session resume 4.32s; Vitest worker-limit probe 4.32s; agent-review cancellation guard 4.08s. The major timed waits remained essentially identical after. Whole-suite improvement stayed below 25% because the change speeds one smaller fixture file, while dominant cases prove real integration timing.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the six slow files and their waits. I optimized the completed one-shot fixture and made the watcher setup event-driven; process startup, lock deadlines, and teardown remain real. I did not change `repoos.toml`, check steps, worker count, release, or close-out logic. After the review changes, two consecutive final-tree `bun run test` runs passed: 708 files, 9,519 passed and 8 skipped each. Their Vitest durations were 296.38s and 221.45s. The final `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` also passed its remote validation, contrast and smoke steps.

## Challenges and blockers

The first final-tree suites under load exposed timeouts in watcher delivery, `agent-review`, and the doctor JSON test while its CLI rebuilt. The watcher miss shared the same class as the fixed 50 ms delay: a one-shot write could precede native watch registration. Both watcher tests now emit repeatable changes until the real signal arrives, then assert the same outcome. I rebuilt before the final full runs; the doctor test then emitted valid JSON. An isolated `agent-review.test.ts` run passed all 17 tests, and two subsequent complete suite runs passed consecutively. The pressure-guard adjustment was removed after the scope note because it was not needed for test speed and belongs to a separate task. The remote runner combines build and tests, so baseline build time cannot be separated from its full validation duration.

## Key learnings

The hottest files are dominated by real process and lock behavior; the safest measured speedup was removing fixture-only idle time without removing cancellation coverage. Filesystem watcher tests should wait for the behavior they assert instead of assuming a fixed startup delay. The top two runtime contributors were left unchanged because `remote-host-pool.test.ts` belongs to #1118 and dev-targets had a parallel-scope conflict; profile data gives those follow-up owners a clear baseline. Runner-load variance is material, so isolated reproduction helps separate load-sensitive failures from regressions.
